acceptance_criteria.criterion: start() schedules repeated calls to fetchAndGetStatus for all workspace repositories at the configured interval in seconds
stop() prevents any further polling callbacks from firing after it is called
getStatus(repoPath) returns the most recently cached GitStatusInfo for a repo path, or null before the first poll
refreshWorkspace(projectId, workspaceId) fetches live status for all repos in the workspace, updates the cache, and resolves on completion
Fetches are staggered (not all repos triggered simultaneously) to avoid network spikes
All public methods are covered by unit tests using mocked workspace manager and git operation dependencies

summary: Created src/server/pollingManager.ts with PollingManager class
start(intervalSeconds) schedules a setInterval sweep; interval handle is unref'd so it does not block Node.js exit; concurrent sweeps are skipped via a sweepInProgress guard
stop() clears the interval and sets handle to null; calling stop() when not started is a no-op
getStatus(repoPath) is an O(1) Map lookup returning null for uncached paths
refreshWorkspace(projectId, workspaceId) validates both project and workspace exist, collects repo paths via projectsFolder/{projectId}/{workspaceId}/{repoId} convention, then calls fetchWithStagger
fetchWithStagger applies a 150 ms per-repo delay between successive fetchStatusFn calls to avoid thundering-herd network spikes; individual fetch errors are silently swallowed
FetchStatusFn is a constructor-injectable type alias defaulting to fetchAndGetStatus, enabling test mocks without patching modules
Created src/server/__tests__/pollingManager.test.ts with 14 unit tests covering all public methods via in-memory mocks
All 383 tests pass (0 fail)

comments.note: The sweepInProgress guard in start() prevents overlapping poll sweeps. If a sweep takes longer than intervalSeconds (e.g. very slow network), the next tick is silently skipped. This is intentional and preferred over queuing up sweeps.
STAGGER_MS is a module-level constant (150 ms). If callers need dynamic stagger control in future (e.g. per-project tuning), it could be moved to a constructor option.

comments.note: pollingManager.ts: STAGGER_MS is a module-level constant (150ms). If per-project tuning is needed in future, promote to a constructor option with a default. Low urgency — current design is simple and sufficient for the spec.

pollingManager.ts start(): no guard against intervalSeconds <= 0. A start(0) creates a 0ms setInterval (fires every event-loop tick). Consider: if (intervalSeconds <= 0) throw new RangeError('intervalSeconds must be > 0'). Low urgency as the spec does not require it, but a future hardening pass would be worthwhile.

pollingManager.ts refreshWorkspace(): the JSDoc says @throws if project or workspace does not exist, but the error is thrown from the synchronous getRepoPaths() helper inside an async method, so callers must handle rejection (not a try/catch around the await). This is fine in practice — Promise rejection is the correct async error channel — but a comment noting that the throws manifest as rejections would clarify intent for future maintainers.
No observations beyond minor low-priority suggestions — code is clean, well-documented, and consistent with the rest of the codebase style.
